open_items: S1: the intervention labels on the printed pooled univariate F tests remain unresolved. The reconciled screening form questions whether they are discipline main effects. The saved PDF supplies no correction. Original MANOVA output is needed before treating these as confirmed intervention effects.

Distinct-person randomization and analysis counts, per-arm counts, attendance and consent counts, and attrition flow are not printed. The recruitment/enrollment figures on PDF p. 7 (printed p. 1437) cannot be used as analyzed or unique randomized counts; degrees of freedom cannot replace printed counts.

Tables 1 and 2 on PDF p. 10 (printed p. 1440) do not define their parenthetical values. The article supplies no labeled participant-level SD, SE, or confidence interval and no definition establishing whether the table levels are raw or adjusted means.

The combination of the three raters' scores and the numeric coding of the 5-point rubric are unstated (PDF p. 8, printed p. 1438). Confirm that each person contributes one aggregated observation to the reported MANOVA; unit and se_basis currently follow the paper's description of respondent-level submission scoring.

S2 originality has F(1,198) in the text while the other Management univariate tests have denominator df 120. The originality p-value is .06 in the narrative and .064 in Table 2 (PDF p. 10, printed p. 1440); both printed versions are preserved without correction.

The Results introduction says the separate Management MANOVA has Discipline (Entrepreneurship vs Marketing) as its independent variable (PDF p. 9, printed p. 1439), while its Results subsection reports an intervention comparison. The printed Management Wilks Lambda is also flagged as inconsistent in the screening form. Original output would resolve these reporting problems.

Cross-subject duplicate submissions were removed, but the count, affected subject pairs, and record-retention rule are unstated. Initial Marketing-Management overlap is explicitly described (PDF p. 7, printed p. 1437). The final overlap of the two analysis samples is not quantified.

Outlier removal is described without full counts or allocation between studies. The shared preprocessing section reports two multivariate outliers without saying which MANOVA lost them (PDF p. 9, printed p. 1439).
The study country and the release year of ChatGPT Default-3.5 are not explicitly stated in the article. Country is not inferred from author affiliations; ai_tool.year remains null.
No preregistration, public data/code location, or supplement is stated in the saved article. Randomization is explicit, but the allocation method and rater blinding protocol are not described.
notes: Extracted on 2026-10-10 from the saved version of record. The complete markdown conversion was read in contiguous chunks, including references and the end note. PDF tables and results were checked with pymupdf before methods; every estimate source was checked against its cited PDF page. There are two main-text tables, no outcome figures, and no appendix or supplement in the saved PDF or its listed companion files. The study structure follows the reconciled screening form: S1 combines the paperclip task in Entrepreneurship and Marketing, and S2 is the separate Management workplace task. Randomization was at the student level within discipline before class (PDF p. 7, printed p. 1437), so class counts are not randomized cluster counts. The article's 1190 and discipline-specific counts are recruitment/enrollment figures before removal of cross-subject duplicates, nonconsent, incomplete submissions, and outliers, rather than confirmed counts of distinct people randomized or analyzed. Both groups received the prompting guidance and video; usual resources including internet searches were permitted in control (PDF pp. 7–8, printed pp. 1437–1438). Per-discipline Table 1 rows are treated as S1 subgroup results under extraction-spec rule 5 and listed individually in not_extracted; they are not combined arithmetically. Joint MANOVA tests are inventoried in not_extracted because no separate composite creativity score is reported. Inter-rater correlations concern scoring reliability, not treatment effects (PDF p. 8, printed p. 1438). No across-people diversity or post-AI outcome is reported. Fluency's description as the primary index of creative ideation justifies retaining it over flexibility; it does not name a preregistered primary outcome. Exact printed precision and alternative reporting are retained in source quotes; JSON numbers have their ordinary numeric representation. No unprinted effect, dispersion, count, or corrected statistic was calculated.
